use_case_changes.setting_proposal: Published comparisons cover one assay's sensitivity against original clinical respiratory panel testing (UCSF SURPI+, 103 of 110), five classifiers on the same 88 respiratory specimens against a 1144-result PCR panel (Carbo et al. 2022), thirteen clinical virology laboratory pipelines on the same 13 clinical datasets (de Vries et al. 2021), and ten submissions on one blood metagenome in the CAMI II pathogen challenge (Meyer et al. 2022). No source compares workflows prospectively on a large cohort with an adjudicated composite reference standard.
evidence_gaps_add: No independent comparison of CZ ID (IDseq), SURPI+, DRAGEN or VirMAP against other workflows on RNA specimens with printed per-tool values was found in this pass.

Carbo et al. 2022's own supplement could not be retrieved (Europe PMC returned a truncated zip, MDPI HTTP 403, PMC a browser challenge); the values come from the medRxiv preprint supplement of the same tables.

The de Vries et al. 2021 published version could not be retrieved (Europe PMC HTTP 500, publisher and three repository copies HTTP 403 or blocked); the preprint and its supplement were used, and its Tables 1 and 2 are images that were not transcribed.
Across the ENNGS benchmark each laboratory used its own reference database and reporting criteria, so tool and database effects cannot be separated.

The COMPARE in silico proficiency test (Brinkmann et al. 2019) scores two highly divergent RNA viruses (measles at 82% and a bornavirus at 55% nucleotide identity) per participant, but participants are anonymised and not linked to named tools, so it was not extracted.
No RNA virus spike-in or reference-material comparison of workflows was found.

exclusions_proposal.proposed: Non-respiratory specimen types, except where a comparison of several workflows on the same data is recorded as proxy evidence and its specimen type is stated (currently CSF, brain biopsy and plasma datasets in the ENNGS benchmark, and one blood metagenome in the CAMI II pathogen challenge)
exclusions_proposal.reason: The two multi-workflow comparisons that separate real detections from background are not respiratory-only: the ENNGS panel is 5 respiratory of 13 datasets, and the CAMI II challenge sample is blood. Keeping the exclusion absolute would drop the only evidence this use case has on contamination and on causal-pathogen calling. Both judgements are proxy and name their specimen types.
exclusions_proposal.if_declined: Drop the meyer2022-cami2-pathogen judgement and mark the two ENNGS judgements outside_scope; the pass then adds only the Carbo et al. respiratory evidence.

use_case_changes.pinned_fields_note: No change is proposed to question, decision, inputs, output, setting or exclusions beyond the two proposals above. These fields are pinned by the existing UCSF judgement (use-case-mapping-amp-20261007-issue14), so changing any of them withholds it until it is reviewed again; if the integrator applies the setting or exclusion change, re-pin that judgement in the same reviewed change.

summary_proposal.source_locator: rna-pathogen-20261009-source-carbo2022-supp: Supplementary Table 1, species level cut-off 0; rna-pathogen-20261009-source-devries2021-supp: Supplementary Tables 2 and 4; rna-pathogen-20261009-source-meyer2022-supp: Supplementary Table 39
summary_proposal.text: On 88 nasal washings scored against 1144 respiratory virus PCR results (Carbo et al. 2022), all five classifiers detected 22 or 23 of the 24 PCR-positive results at species level (sensitivity 0.9167, or 0.9583 for Kaiju), but between 33% and 58% of their positive calls were PCR-negative: species-level PPV was 0.42 to 0.69 with human reads kept, and 0.52 to 0.67 after removing them. Removing human reads raised specificity for every classifier except CLARK, whose sensitivity fell to 0.8333. When 13 European laboratories each ran their own pipeline on the same 13 clinical datasets (de Vries et al. 2021), 10 to 13 of the 13 samples were correctly called positive, and the pipelines that found every sample (DNASTAR, FEVIR, MetaMix) reported 0 to 6 additional viruses whose PCR was negative, so their hit-level PPV ranged from 71.4% to 100%. Rotavirus, reported in one sample by most pipelines, was also present in a negative run control the participants never saw. In the CAMI II clinical pathogen challenge on one blood metagenome (Meyer et al. 2022), 4 of 10 submissions listed the causal virus and 3 named it as causal. None of this is clinical validation: the respiratory cohort has 24 positive results, the ENNGS panel mixes specimen types and includes DNA virus targets, every laboratory used its own database and reporting rules, and the CAMI submissions were manually curated and not reproducible.

number_trace.22 or 23 of 24: Derived from those sensitivities and the 24 PCR-positive results in the dataset record (0.9167 x 24 = 22, 0.9583 x 24 = 23)
number_trace.PPV 0.42 to 0.69 and 0.52 to 0.67: rna-pathogen-20261009-result-carbo2022-species-cutoff-0-<tool>-{incl,excl}-human-ppv (0.4151 Centrifuge to 0.6875 CLARK; 0.5227 Kaiju to 0.6667 CLARK and Genome Detective)
number_trace.33% to 58% of positive calls PCR-negativ: One minus the same PPV values
number_trace.10 to 13 of 13 samples: rna-pathogen-20261009-result-devries2021-sample-<pipeline>-correct (10 for DAMIAN, Jovian, MetaMIC and One Codex; 13 for DNAstar, FEVIR and MetaMix)
number_trace.0 to 6 additional viruses, PPV 71.4% to: rna-pathogen-20261009-result-devries2021-hit-<pipeline>-fp and -ppv (DNAstar 6 and 71.42857142857143; FEVIR 2 and 88.23529411764706; MetaMix 0 and 100)
number_trace.4 of 10 listed and 3 named it causal: rna-pathogen-20261009-result-meyer2022-<submission>-in-list and -predicted-causal (yes for Bracken v2.2, Bracken v2.5, MetaPhlAn v2.2.0 and CCMetagen v1.1.3 in the list; causal yes for Bracken v2.2, MetaPhlAn v2.2.0 and CCMetagen v1.1.3, as Supplementary Table 39 prints them)

summary_proposal.caveat_note: The CAMI counts follow Supplementary Table 39. The article text swaps the two Bracken versions; that conflict is recorded as an evidence concern on the supplement source.

gaps: No prospective clinical cohort with an adjudicated composite reference standard and several workflows.
Hosted clinical RNA pipelines (CZ ID, SURPI+, DRAGEN, VirMAP) have no independent head-to-head table in this pass.
Carbo et al. genus and family sheets were extracted, but the published supplement was not retrievable.
de Vries et al. Tables 1 and 2 (pipeline characteristics and read-count categories) are images in the preprint and were not transcribed, so version and database detail per pipeline is unextracted.
Brinkmann et al. 2019 (divergent RNA viruses, anonymised participants) not extracted.
CAMI II Supplementary Fig. 16 (taxa per submission) is a figure and was not read.
No result is comparable across the three sources: specimens, databases, reporting rules and scoring differ.
concerns_for_reviewer: Carbo et al. Supplementary Table 1 prints 10000 in eight cells for quantities bounded by 0 and 1 (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV). These are probably 1.0000 with the decimal point lost. printed_value keeps 10000, numeric_value is null, and each carries source_anomaly. No evidence concern was raised on the source because the reading is a transcription artefact rather than a disputed value; a reviewer may prefer one.

The Carbo et al. column headed 'Informedness' holds the ROC distance to the error-free point, not Youden's J: Section 2.7 defines it that way, and for all 56 rows with in-range values the printed number equals sqrt((1-SN)^2 + (1-SL)^2) within rounding. Recorded as metric roc-distance with the printed label in source_label and a claim.
Carbo et al. gives the Genome Detective version as 1.126 in Table 2 and its database as version 1.130 in Section 2.5. Both are recorded in the configuration version field.
The meaning of the 0 and 10 read cut-offs alongside the ROC-selected threshold is not defined beyond a sheet note; the two species blocks are kept as separate protocols.

de Vries et al. Supplementary Table 2 has 14 pipeline rows including 'DIAMOND pipeline 3A', while the Methods say 13 pipelines and that DAMIAN was run by two participants as A and B. Evidence concern recorded on the supplement source; the row is kept as its own configuration with no summary values.

de Vries et al.'s abstract gives the lowest sample-level sensitivity as 80% (10/13); 10/13 is 76.9%, which is what the Results text and Supplementary Table 2 print. 80% matches the lowest hit-level value (12/15). Part of the same evidence concern.

ENNGS pipelines developed at participating laboratories are recorded as author_reported; Centrifuge and the four commercial platforms as independent_paper; DAMIAN as unreported because the source does not say whether participants developed it.

CAMI II Supplementary Table 39 and the article text disagree on which Bracken version predicted the causal pathogen. Evidence concern on the supplement source; table values recorded. The CAMI results are categorical yes/no on one sample, stored as metric success-rate with a null numeric_value and the criterion in attributes.criterion.

Whether the Carbo et al. species and genus judgements should be direct (as recorded) or proxy: the cohort is the use case's specimen type and the targets are RNA respiratory viruses, but the reference is the original PCR panel rather than an adjudicated standard.
Whether to broaden the non-respiratory exclusion, as proposed in use_case_changes.exclusions_proposal.
